title: Living Things
bigQuestion: How are animals different from each other?
summary: Students learn words for creatures and their homes, use the present passive (Insects are eaten by birds.) and where clauses (The desert is where camels live.), and practice controlling anger.
warmup: What is your favorite animal? Why?
Which animals can you see in Saudi Arabia?
Which is heavier, a camel or a tortoise?
What can you do when you feel angry?

grammar.title: Present Passive
grammar.rule: We use the passive when the action is more important than who does it. Make it with am / is / are + past participle. Add “by” to say who does the action.
grammar.form: subject + am / is / are (not) + past participle (+ by ...)
examples: Tortoises aren't found in very cold places.
Is this nest built by eagles?

items.prompt: Small fish ___ by octopuses.
items.explanation: “Small fish” is plural, so we use are + eaten.

items.prompt: This nest ___ by an eagle.
items.explanation: “This nest” is one thing, so we use is + built.

items.prompt: Dinosaur bones ___ by scientists.
items.explanation: “Bones” is plural: are + past participle (studied).

items.prompt: Which sentence is passive?
options: Camels are found in the desert.
Camels drink a lot of water.
items.answer: Camels are found in the desert.
items.explanation: A passive sentence has am / is / are + past participle: are found.

items.prompt: Swans ___ in the desert.
items.explanation: Negative passive with a plural subject: aren't (are not) + seen.

items.prompt: ___ honey made by bees?
items.explanation: Passive questions start with Is / Are. “Honey” is one thing, so we use Is.

items.prompt: Leaves ___ by tortoises.
items.explanation: Plural subject (leaves) + are + eaten.

items.prompt: In spring, our garden ___ by many butterflies.
items.explanation: “Our garden” is one thing: is + visited.

items.prompt: Eagles ___ in the ocean.
items.explanation: Negative passive: are not (aren't) + found. Find → found.

items.prompt: This small red beetle ___ a ladybug.
items.explanation: We say a thing “is called” + its name.

items.prompt: Wild animals ___ at the animal center.
items.explanation: Plural subject: are + looked after.

items.prompt: The school pond ___ every week.
items.explanation: “The pond” is one thing: is + cleaned. We don't need “by” because who cleans it isn't important.

items.answer: Insects are eaten by many birds.
items.explanation: Passive: subject + are + past participle + by + who does it.

items.answer: Butterflies are seen in our garden.
items.explanation: Passive: Butterflies + are seen + where.

items.answer: Is the camel looked after by Fahad?
items.explanation: Passive question: Is + subject + past participle + by ...?

items.answer: Tortoises are not found in cold places.
items.explanation: Negative passive: are not + found.

items.prompt: Bees make honey.
items.explanation: The object (honey) becomes the subject: Honey is made by bees.

items.prompt: Birds eat insects.
items.explanation: Insects is plural, so: Insects are eaten by birds.

items.prompt: Scientists study dinosaurs.

Riyadh Zoo is visited by many people.

Passive needs the past participle: made, not make.

items.sentence: The eggs are kept warm by the mother bird.
items.answer: The eggs are kept warm by the mother bird.
items.explanation: Correct! Plural subject + are + kept.

items.sentence: Camels is found in the desert.
items.answer: Camels are found in the desert.
items.explanation: “Camels” is plural, so we use are, not is.
Don't forget am / is / are in a passive sentence.

items.sentence: This butterfly are seen in spring.
items.answer: This butterfly is seen in spring.
items.explanation: “This butterfly” is one thing, so we use is.

grammar.title: Where Clauses
grammar.rule: We use “where” to talk about a place and what happens there. After the place, say “is where” or “are where”, then a full sentence with a subject and a verb.
grammar.form: place + is / are + where + subject + verb
examples: The desert is where camels live.
A nest is where eagles lay their eggs.
A pond is where frogs and swans swim.
The museum is where we saw the dinosaur bones.

items.prompt: A nest is ___ birds keep their eggs.
items.explanation: We use “where” to talk about a place.

items.prompt: The ocean is where octopuses ___.
items.explanation: After “where” we need subject + verb: octopuses live.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: The pond is where ducks swim.
The pond is where swim ducks.
The pond where is ducks swim.
items.answer: The pond is where ducks swim.
items.explanation: The order is: place + is where + subject + verb.

items.prompt: A zoo is where ___.
items.explanation: After “where” we need a full sentence with a subject and a verb.

items.prompt: The mountains are where eagles ___ found.
items.explanation: “Eagles” is plural, so the passive is are found.

items.prompt: Choose the best ending: “A beehive is where ...”
items.explanation: A beehive is the home of bees, where they make honey.

items.prompt: A desert is ___ it is very hot and dry.
items.explanation: We use “where” to describe a place.

items.prompt: The sea is where sharks and octopuses ___.
items.explanation: Plural subject (sharks and octopuses) + live.

items.prompt: A nest is where a bird ___ its eggs.
items.explanation: “A bird” is one: a bird lays.

items.prompt: The pond is where we ___ the swans yesterday.
items.explanation: “Yesterday” is the past, so see → saw.

items.prompt: A zoo ___ where people look at animals.
items.explanation: “A zoo” is one place: A zoo is where ...

items.prompt: Old trees are ___ many beetles live.
items.explanation: Trees are a place here, so we use where.

reading.title: Creatures in Grandma's Garden
reading.text:
Every Friday, Nouf and her little brother Omar visit their grandmother in Taif. Her garden is full of flowers, trees and small creatures.

This Friday, Omar wants to find a dinosaur. “Dinosaurs are extinct,” Nouf laughs. “But look! This beetle looks like a tiny dinosaur.” The beetle has a hard, shiny back and six legs.

Then a beautiful butterfly lands on a rose. Omar runs to touch it, but it flies away. He is very angry. He shouts and kicks the grass.

Grandma sits next to him. “When I feel angry, I stop and take three deep breaths,” she says quietly. “Butterflies are frightened by loud noises. Calm, quiet children see more creatures.”

Omar takes three deep breaths. Soon he feels better. He sits very still, and two butterflies land near him. Then Grandma's old tortoise walks out from under a bush. Its shell is heavy, so it moves very slowly. Omar does not touch it. He just watches.

“This garden is the best zoo in the world!” Omar whispers.

reading.title: Where Do Animals Live?
reading.text:
Every animal needs the right home. The place where an animal lives is called its environment. Let's visit four different environments.

The desert is where camels live. It is hot and dry, and there is not much water. Camels can go on long journeys for many days without drinking. Their thick fur keeps the hot sun off their skin.

The ocean is where octopuses live. An octopus has eight arms and no bones, so it can hide in very small holes between rocks. Octopuses are eaten by sharks and big fish, so hiding is very important for them.

A pond is a small area of water. It is where frogs lay their eggs and swans swim. Swans are big white birds with long necks. Baby swans are looked after by both parents.

High mountains are where eagles build their nests. An eagle's nest is made of sticks, and it can be very big and heavy. Eagles have strong wings and very good eyes. They can see a small animal from far away.

reading.title: A Night in the Desert
reading.text:
Saturday, January 12

Dear Diary,

This weekend, my family went camping in the desert. The journey from Riyadh took two hours by car. The desert is where my grandfather grew up, so he knows a lot about it.

In the afternoon, we went for a walk. Grandpa showed me some small tracks in the sand. “These tracks are made by beetles,” he said. Then we found one. It was black and shiny, and it looked like a little stone with legs!

Next, we saw a lizard under a bush. I wanted to touch it, but Grandpa said, “Wild animals are not pets. Just watch them.” So I just watched it quietly. The shade under a bush is where many lizards rest in the hot afternoon.

In the evening, we sat near the fire. The desert was very quiet. Grandpa told me that many desert creatures are not seen in the day. They sleep in holes, and they come out at night to look for insects and seeds.

Later, a small furry fox walked near our tent! Its big ears help it to hear insects under the sand. It looked at us for a minute and then ran away.

What an amazing weekend! I want to come back next year.

Lama

reading.title: The Arabian Leopard
reading.text:
What is it?
The Arabian leopard is a big wild cat. It is the largest cat in Arabia. Its fur is light yellow with black spots. Its body is strong, but it is not very heavy. An adult male weighs about 30 kilograms.

Where does it live?
Rocky mountains are where Arabian leopards live. They like quiet places far away from people. A cave is where a mother leopard keeps her babies safe.

What does it eat?
Leopards are hunters. Rabbits, birds and wild goats are hunted by leopards, usually at night.

Is it in danger?
Yes. There are very few Arabian leopards in the wild today. If we don't protect them, this beautiful creature may become extinct, like the dinosaurs.

How is it protected?
In Saudi Arabia, leopards are looked after in a special center in Taif. Baby leopards are born there, and they are fed by experts every day. In the future, some leopards may go back to the mountains near AlUla.

Did you know?
A leopard can climb trees very well. It often carries its food up a tree. A high branch is where other animals can't take its dinner!

reading.title: Busy Bees in the Mountains
reading.text:
For our science project, Reem interviewed her uncle, Mr. Saeed. He keeps bees in the mountains near Abha.

Reem: Uncle Saeed, why do you like bees?
Mr. Saeed: Bees are amazing insects! They have four wings, and they work very hard. Without bees, many fruits and flowers can't grow.

Reem: Where do your bees live?
Mr. Saeed: A wild bee's nest is often found inside an old tree. But these wooden boxes are where my bees live. Each box is called a hive. About 40,000 bees live in one hive!

Reem: Is the honey made by all the bees?
Mr. Saeed: No. The honey is made by worker bees. The queen bee lays the eggs. She is looked after by the workers. They feed her and keep her clean.

Reem: Can I touch a bee?
Mr. Saeed: No, please don't! If a bee is frightened, it can sting. Bees like calm, quiet people. When I work, I wear special clothes, and I move slowly.

Reem: What do the bees do in winter?
Mr. Saeed: They stay inside the hive and keep warm together. They make a big ball, like a furry blanket!

Reem: Thank you, Uncle Saeed!
Mr. Saeed: You're welcome. Now let's taste some honey!

wordWork.title: Understanding Present Passive syntax
wordWork.rule: In an active sentence, the subject does the action (Bees make honey.). In a passive sentence, the object moves to the front and “by” tells us who does the action (Honey is made by bees.).

items.prompt: “Insects are eaten by birds.” Who does the eating?
items.explanation: The word after “by” tells us who does the action: birds.

items.prompt: “The nest is built by the eagle.” What is built?
items.explanation: In a passive sentence, the thing at the front receives the action: the nest.

items.prompt: Active: Bees make honey. Passive: Honey is made ___ bees.
items.explanation: We use “by” to say who does the action.

items.prompt: What is the past participle of “eat”?
items.explanation: eat – ate – eaten. The passive uses the third form: eaten.

items.prompt: Fish ___ eaten by eagles.
items.explanation: “Fish” here means many fish, so we use are.

items.prompt: Which word shows who does the action in a passive sentence?
items.explanation: “By” comes before the person or animal who does the action.

items.prompt: Active: People see camels in the desert. Passive: Camels are ___ in the desert.
items.explanation: see – saw – seen. The passive uses seen.

items.prompt: Choose the ACTIVE sentence.
items.explanation: In the active sentence, the doer (tortoises) comes first and there is no is / are + past participle.

items.prompt: Wild camels are ___ in the desert.
items.explanation: find – found – found. The passive is are found.

writing.prompt: Write a description of an animal environment.
writing.hint: Use: ... is where ..., ... are found in ..., is / are + past participle.
writing.model: The ocean is where many amazing creatures live. It is big, deep and blue. Octopuses are found between the rocks, and small fish are seen everywhere. Sea turtles swim slowly through the water. Many small fish are eaten by sharks, so they swim together in big groups. The Red Sea near Jeddah is where I want to go diving one day.

writing.prompt: Describe an animal and its traits.
writing.hint: What does it look like? Where is it found? What does it eat? Use: It looks like ..., It has ..., It is found in ...
writing.model: My favorite animal is the eagle. It is a big bird with strong wings and sharp eyes. Eagles are found in the mountains, where they build their nests. Small animals are hunted by eagles. An eagle's nest is made of sticks. I think eagles look strong and beautiful.
